chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'Those firmly rooted in knowledge' are the Commander of the Faithful and the Imams after him (peace be upon them).

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful — a title specific to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ: Those firmly rooted in knowledge — a Quranic phrase from 3:7 denoting those with deep and stable understanding of divine scripture

ai.seo_question: Who are 'those firmly rooted in knowledge' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the Quranic phrase 'those firmly rooted in knowledge' (al-rasikhun fi al-'ilm) from Surah Al 'Imran (3:7) as specifically referring to Imam Ali (AS) and the subsequent Imams (AS). This hadith is part of a broader Shia theological tradition that interprets Quranic verses about special knowledge and authority as referring to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt. The audience — the companions and students of Imam al-Sadiq — would have understood this as asserting that the Imams possess the deepest comprehension of the Quran, including its ambiguous verses (mutashabihat).
